![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224770/assets/179894a17a2aadf5ba9f463ae3faf2e5836f7b268066f8f56de0f3cf3ff2d8fa.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(2-x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=2.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}x(2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2{x}^{3}-{x}^{4})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
